recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This image shows NGC 520, which looks like a single galaxy but is really two disk galaxies in collision. Their encounter began more than 300 million years ago, and the pair will eventually merge into one larger, more massive system.

NGC 520 lies in the direction of Pisces. William Herschel discovered it in 1784, and the Siena Galaxy Atlas lists it among its largest and brightest galaxies. Galaxy collisions unfold slowly. The stars themselves rarely hit one another, because the space between them is so vast. Instead, gravity reshapes the galaxies, pulling out streams of stars and stirring up gas and dust, which can set off new bursts of star formation.
The image was taken with the Dark Energy Camera on the NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope through g, r and z filters, as part of observations led by J. Moustakas of Siena College.
